div.div: 4 آرَطَتِ الأَرْضُ , (AHeyth, K,) of the measure أَفْعَلَت, [originally] with two alifs, (TA,) [aor. يُؤْرِطُ, inf. n. إِيرَاطٌ,] The land produced the kind of trees called أَرْطًى [or أَرْطَى]; (AHeyth, K;) as also أَرْطَت, inf. n. إِرْطَآءٌ; or this is a corruption, attributable to J: so says the author of the K, following AHeyth: but it is no corruption, for it is mentioned by the authors on verbs and by ISd and others; (MF, TA;) for instance, by AHn, in his book on plants, and by IF, in the Mj: (TA:) [and J mentions it in its proper place, in art. رطى, as well as in the present art.:] ↓ أَرَّطَت , with the ر musheddedeh, has also been found in the handwriting of certain of the men of letters; but this is a corruption. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
